distractors.reason: 'Hardly' means 'almost not' or 'barely'. 'Work hardly' would suggest not working enough, which changes the meaning.
'Heavily' describes weight or a large amount (it rained heavily). We don't say 'work heavily'.
'Strictly' means 'in a rigid or precise way' (follow the rules strictly). It doesn't mean 'with great effort'.

example_sentence: Our sales team will have to work ___ to reach the target this quarter.
l1_interference: Osoby mówiące po polsku często stawiają przysłówek przed czasownikiem, jak w 'ciężko pracować', i mogą powiedzieć 'I hard work every day' zamiast 'I work hard every day'. Po angielsku przysłówek zwykle stoi po czasowniku.
explanation: In English, the adverb 'hard' usually comes after the verb: 'work hard', 'try hard', 'study hard'. Placing it before the verb sounds unnatural.

related_collocations.example: She speaks English fluently after two years in London.
Please listen carefully to the instructions.
They negotiated successfully and signed the contract.

memory_tip: HARD = with great effort (work hard, try hard) | HARDLY = almost not (hardly ever, hardly any)
